Mandatory Enrollment and Overview
All international students who stay in Korea must enroll in the National Health Isurance Service(NHIS).
Generally, eligibility for NHIS begins once you have completed your ARC. The NHIS will send a bill or notice of enrollment.
The monthly premium for international students is approximately KRW 70,000-80,000.
NHIS covers a large portion of costs for medical treatment, precripstions, and check-ups. Certain services such as cosmetic procedures, some dental treatments, and elective surgeries may not be covered.
Payment and Usage
Monthly insurance bills are seny by mail. Payment can be made via bank transfer, internet banking, or automatic withdrawal.
When visiting clinics or hostpitals, show your ARC or insurance card to recevie the NHIS discount.
Exemptions from NHIS
Some international students may be eligible to opt out of or be exempted from mandatory NHIS under specific conditions recognized by the NHIS. For example, you may request an exemption if you meet any of the criteria below:
Valid Private Health Insurance: You hold a private or government sponsored health insurance plan that provides coverage equivalent to (or greather than) Korea's NHIS. Evidence of sufficient coverage must be submitted to the NHIS.
Reciprocal Social Security Agreement: Your Home country may have a bilateral/multilateral social security agreement with Korea, which allows certain categories of exchange students or workers to be exempted. Verify with your home country's authority or the NHIS if this applied to you.
Documentation & Deadlines: To apply for an exemption, you usually need to submit documentation (insurance certificate, policy details, etc.) to a local NHIS office within a specific time frame. If appoved, you will not be billed by the NHIS for that period of exemption.
